name: Nowhere Station

stars.name: Nowhere Station
stars.notes: Active M-dwarf at the bright end of its class. Occasional flares and a strong stellar wind, but relatively stable luminosity output overall.

planets.name: Berth
planets.notes: Tidally locked world with extreme thermal gradients. The terminator zone shows unusual mineral banding — alternating layers of crystallized silicates formed by repeated heating and cooling cycles.

planets.name: Layover
planets.notes: Marginal habitable-zone world with a nitrogen-CO2 atmosphere at 1.4 atm surface pressure. Temperatures hover near freezing at the equator. Liquid water exists in sheltered equatorial basins during perihelion.

planets.name: Departure
planets.notes: Ice giant with a distinctive pale green coloration from methane and ammonia absorption. Its three moons are geologically diverse, with the largest showing signs of past tidal heating.

asteroid_belts.name: Transit Rubble
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin belt of mixed-composition debris. Water-ice content is notably high, making it a potential resupply source for hydrogen-oxygen fuel if a depot were ever established.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. Located along the Holloway Transit corridor but has not been developed as a waypoint. The name is aspirational — there is no actual station here.

history: Nowhere Station was surveyed in 2521 alongside Waypoint Null as part of the Holloway Transit route planning initiative. It ranked marginally higher than Waypoint Null due to accessible water ice in the asteroid belt but was still not selected for waystation development.

The system acquired its ironic name from transit pilots who noted the coordinates in their charts with the annotation 'station planned' that never materialized. Over time, the placeholder became the official name — a station that exists only as a name on a map.

Occasional transit vessels passing through the Holloway corridor have used the system for emergency resupply, harvesting water ice from the Transit Rubble belt. These visits are infrequent and undocumented, leaving no permanent trace.
description: Nowhere Station is a three-planet system orbiting an active red-orange dwarf along the Holloway Transit corridor. The system is compact — Berth bakes in close orbit, Layover sits at the edge of habitability with seasonal liquid water, and Departure hangs farther out as a pale green ice giant. The asteroid belt between the inner and outer system is sparse but water-rich, the one resource that gives Nowhere Station any practical relevance at all.

The system's name is its own commentary. Nowhere Station was supposed to be somewhere — a refueling waypoint along the long, empty Holloway passage between two distant sectors of colonized space. The waystation was planned, budgeted, and then cancelled when political priorities shifted. The name stuck as a joke among transit pilots: a place on every chart that contains nothing when you arrive. Ships occasionally stop to crack ice from the asteroid belt when fuel runs low, but these are acts of desperation rather than planned logistics.

Layover's seasonal liquid water makes it a marginal candidate for future development. During perihelion, equatorial basins fill with shallow, briny lakes that persist for weeks before freezing again — a cycle that has repeated for billions of years without sparking life. If the Holloway corridor ever sees enough traffic to justify infrastructure, Nowhere Station might finally live up to its name. Until then, it remains the transit stop that never was, a set of coordinates marking empty space and unkept promises.
